http_semantics.note: 1001 points exceeds contract upper bound of 1000, but server returns HTTP 200 with success status. Server accepted invalid batch size without rejection.

chain_trace.break_detail: contract asserts len(points) <= 1000; server received request with 1001 points but returned HTTP 200 with operation_id=1, status='acknowledged'; server did not reject the oversized batch. Server-side validation at verification/update.rs:165-169 uses check_limit_opt() with strict_mode_config.upsert_max_batchsize, but this is a configurable limit that defaults to None/unbounded, not an absolute maximum of 1000. Chain断裂在log层：服務器接受了違反契約上限的請求並返回成功。

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST API: schema.rs defines PointsList/PointsBatch without length(max = 1000) validation → request deserialization succeeds for 1001 points → verification/update.rs:check_custom() calls check_limit_opt() with strict_mode_config.upsert_max_batchsize → if upsert_max_batchsize is None/unbounded, check_limit_opt returns Ok(()) at line 342-344 → request proceeds to handler → server processes all 1001 points and returns HTTP 200 → contract violation: len(points) <= 1000 not enforced

mundane_explanation.surviving: Type1 violation - API should reject batches exceeding 1000 points with 400 Bad Request per contract, but server accepts 1001 points and returns HTTP 200 success. Validation is configurable (strict_mode_config.upsert_max_batchsize) rather than absolute (1000), allowing oversized batches to pass through when limit is not configured or set too high.
